ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation, bank onboarding, and material transactions, screen all shareholders, directors, authorized signatories, UBOs, and relevant counterparties against United Nations sanctions, European Union sanctions, Spanish domestic sanctions, and OFAC lists as a risk-control measure. Apply Spanish PEP rules under Law 10/2010 and Royal Decree 304/2014, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, senior-management approval, enhanced ongoing monitoring, and family or close-associate review where applicable. Obtain documentary evidence of ownership through the full control chain to natural persons; apply the senior-managing-official fallback only after reasonable ownership and control investigations are documented. Screen adverse media, insolvency, litigation, corruption, fraud, customs, tax, and food-safety records. Do not rely solely on name matching; resolve aliases, transliterations, dates of birth, nationality, and corporate identifiers. Spanish regulated entities must maintain AML records for the statutory retention period, generally ten years under Law 10/2010.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry), official online services at https://www.rmc.es/
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be unique and distinguishable from existing names and must include the legal-form designation or its accepted abbreviation, such as Sociedad Limitada, Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada, S.L., or S.R.L. The name may be in Spanish or another permitted language, but it must not mislead as to the company's activity, legal form, or public status. Foreign words, acronyms, and transliterations are permitted subject to distinctiveness, public-order limitations, and registry acceptance. The RMC issues the negative-name certificate required for incorporation. The notarial deed and registry filings are generally in Spanish, or in the applicable co-official language where accepted by the relevant authority.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Existing or confusingly similar registered company names
Terms implying a public authority, official institution, or sovereign function, including Estado, Gobierno, Ministerio, Ayuntamiento, Comunidad Autónoma, and Unión Europea
Bank, Banco, Banca, Caja, Crédito, Financiera, Seguros, Aseguradora, Bolsa, Valores, and other regulated-financial terms unless legally justified and authorized
Terms implying regulated professional, educational, medical, pharmaceutical, securities, insurance, or public-service activities without the required authorization
Spain, España, Spanish, Española, Real, Imperial, National, Nacional, official territorial names, and other terms potentially requiring documentary justification or prior administrative approval
Abusive, discriminatory, unlawful, defamatory, or public-order-inconsistent expressions
Words that misrepresent the company's legal form, ownership, activity, or relationship with a public body
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: File the name application electronically or through an authorized intermediary with the RMC, submitting up to five proposed names in priority order. Following issuance, use the original negative-name certificate in the incorporation deed. The certificate is generally valid for three months from issuance for execution of the deed; the underlying name reservation may remain protected for the applicable statutory period, commonly six months, subject to RMC rules. If rejected, obtain the written registry reason, verify similarity and sensitive-term grounds, revise the proposed names, and refile. Where the rejection is legally contestable, submit a reasoned administrative challenge or request for reconsideration to the competent RMC body within the applicable procedural deadline, attaching evidence of distinctiveness, authorization, or legitimate use. A subsequent judicial challenge before the competent commercial or administrative court may be available depending on the nature of the decision. Rejection does not authorize use of the name before a valid certificate is issued.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A Spanish SL must have a registered office in Spain under the Companies Act. A serviced or virtual office may be acceptable for corporate-registration and correspondence purposes if it provides a genuine address, reliable receipt and forwarding of official notices, and landlord or provider authorization. It is not sufficient where the company conducts manufacturing, food handling, warehousing, packaging, importation, or distribution from another site. Canned or ambient tapioca-pearl manufacturing requires appropriate premises, food-hygiene controls, traceability, equipment, environmental and municipal compliance, and registration or notification with the competent food-safety authorities. A virtual office should therefore be limited to the registered-office function and not presented as the manufacturing or operational establishment.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated medium-to-high operational inspection risk for the manufacturing activity, approximately 20%-40% annually during the first three years where the company operates a food-production facility, imports food ingredients, or files for food-business registration; this is a non-statutory risk estimate and not a guaranteed frequency. Risk increases materially following complaints, non-compliance findings, unusual import activity, incomplete traceability, labeling deficiencies, or high-risk products. Registered-office-only inspections are less likely but remain possible for tax, registry, AML, or local-authority verification.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), approved by Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010, including Articles 4, 20-24, 32-35, 58-62, 159-197, 209-252, and 285-290. The Companies Registry framework also includes the Commercial Registry Regulations approved by Royal Decree 1784/1996.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) of the province of the registered office, coordinated nationally through the Central Commercial Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución) containing the articles of association, followed by registration with the applicable Provincial Commercial Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: An Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada may be incorporated with capital of at least EUR 1. Where capital is below EUR 3,000, statutory reserve and creditor-protection rules apply, including allocation of at least 20% of annual profit until the reserve plus capital reaches EUR 3,000 and shareholder liability for the difference upon liquidation if company assets are insufficient. Contributions must be fully assumed and paid at incorporation. Spain does not require a general capital escrow account, although a bank certificate or equivalent evidence of contribution may be requested where cash is contributed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board resolves to confirm the subscription and full payment of the entire share capital described in the incorporation deed, with each share issued, subscribed, and paid in accordance with the articles. The Board adopts as the Company’s registered office the address stated in the deed and authorizes its filing with the Provincial Commercial Registry. The Board appoints the persons identified in the deed as directors and, where applicable, appoints the managing director and other officers, with the powers permitted by law and the articles. The secretary is authorized to execute all ancillary filings, certifications, and banking instructions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central), through its online name-certification service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to five proposed names and obtain a valid negative name certificate. Ensure the proposed name includes the legal form designation or its accepted abbreviation, "S.L.". The certificate should generally be issued in the name of a founder or authorized incorporator and presented to the notary within its validity period.
required_dossiers: Up to five proposed company names
Power of attorney, if submitted by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is rejected, submit an alternative name or correct the proposed name based on the Registry objection. If the certificate expires, obtain a renewed certificate before execution of the incorporation deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary public selected for execution of the incorporation deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the articles of association, business purpose, registered office, share capital, share allocation, governance structure, director appointments, and beneficial-ownership information. Foreign shareholders and directors must obtain Spanish tax identification numbers where required. Legalized and apostilled foreign documents must be accompanied by sworn Spanish translations unless an applicable exemption applies.
required_dossiers: Founders’ identity documents and tax identification numbers
Evidence of cash contribution or description and valuation of non-cash contributions
Registered-office evidence or owner consent where requested
Foreign corporate certificates, apostilles, and sworn translations where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure missing identification, legalization, translation, ownership, or capital evidence before signing. Obtain a supplemental notarial instrument if an executed deed contains a remediable clerical or documentary defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the escritura pública de constitución. The notary verifies capacity, identity, powers, corporate name, articles, capital subscription, contribution payment, and beneficial ownership. The deed must identify the first directors and include the statutory corporate particulars. The notary or authorized representative should electronically transmit the deed to the Commercial Registry without undue delay.
required_dossiers: Original or valid electronic negative name certificate
Powers of attorney and legalized foreign documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct notarial observations before execution. If the Registry later identifies a defect, execute a corrective or supplementary deed and resubmit it within the applicable presentation priority period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Tax Identification and Register the Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria) and the Provincial Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the provisional corporate tax identification number through the Tax Agency using Form 036, then file the notarized deed, articles, tax identification evidence, and required registry forms with the Provincial Commercial Registry. After registration, obtain the definitive tax identification number and update the Tax Agency record. Submit beneficial-ownership information through the channels required by the notarial and registry systems.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the registrar’s qualification notice by correcting the identified defect, supplying missing documents, or filing a corrective deed. A negative qualification may be challenged through the statutory Commercial Registry appeal or judicial review procedures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Post-Incorporation Corporate and Employment Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Agency, General Treasury of Social Security, and applicable regional and municipal authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm definitive tax registration, select the accounting and corporate books, legalize books electronically through the Commercial Registry, register as an employer before hiring personnel, obtain Social Security affiliation and contribution codes, and file the commencement-of-activity information. Establish accounting, invoicing, data-protection, workplace-risk, and food-traceability controls before operations begin.
required_dossiers: Employer registration and Social Security documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify tax or Social Security registration data through the relevant electronic filing channel. Do not commence regulated manufacturing or employ personnel until mandatory registrations, municipal authorizations, and safety controls are effective.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: The Industry Directorate or equivalent industrial authority of the Autonomous Community where the plant is located, together with the competent municipality, the regional food-safety authority, and the Spanish Agency for Food Safety and Nutrition (AESAN) for national coordination. There is no single national industrial licensing board for all food manufacturing facilities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registration in the General Health Registry of Food and Food Businesses (Registro General Sanitario de Empresas Alimentarias y Alimentos, RGSEAA) under Royal Decree 191/2011, plus the applicable municipal opening or activity authorization and any regional environmental authorization. Industrial-establishment registration under Royal Decree 559/2010 may also apply depending on the installation and Autonomous Community requirements.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Competent environmental authority of the relevant Autonomous Community, applying the Environmental Assessment Act (Law 21/2013) and regional implementing rules
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Normally subject to a project-specific screening assessment or regional environmental authorization analysis; a full EIA is not automatically required solely because the activity manufactures ambient tapioca pearls. The final classification depends on plant capacity, location, water use, emissions, waste, protected-area status, and applicable Annex thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Obtain a municipal or regional wastewater discharge authorization where required and comply with applicable sewer or receiving-water limits under the Water Law framework and Royal Decree 849/1986. Control suspended solids, organic load, pH, temperature, oils, and other parameters specified in the discharge permit. Comply with Royal Decree 117/2003 for solvent-related VOC emissions where its activity and consumption thresholds are met. Segregate, label, store, and transfer waste through authorized operators under Law 7/2022 and its implementing rules; maintain traceability for food waste, packaging, sludge, and hazardous waste.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before opening, obtain the applicable municipal activity or opening authorization and fire-safety approval. Design and certify the plant under the applicable Building Code fire provisions and industrial fire-safety regulations, including emergency routes, compartmentation, extinguishing systems, fire detection, and inspection requirements. Complete structural load and machinery-installation certifications where applicable. Comply with the Occupational Risk Prevention Act (Law 31/1995), workplace health and safety regulations, food-hygiene requirements under Regulation (EC) No. 852/2004, HACCP-based procedures, potable-water controls, pest control, worker training, and documented commissioning inspections.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); e-Portal: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL), obtain a provisional NIF from AEAT after notarizing the incorporation deed and filing with the Mercantile Registry; final definitive NIF is issued via Form 036/030. Non-resident entities establishing a permanent establishment apply through AEAT Form 030/036 with a legal representative, notarized powers of attorney, and translated corporate documents. The NIF serves simultaneously as the Corporate Tax ID and VAT ID.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists; Spanish resident SLs are mandatorily subject to Corporate Income Tax on worldwide income. Optional elections include the consolidated tax group regime for parent companies holding at least 75% of subsidiaries, the qualifying Spanish International Holding regime (ETVE), and the 15% preferential CIT rate for newly created SLs in the first two tax periods. Hybrid mismatch rules are applied under EU ATAD; they are not elective.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general de minimis/threshold registration: any taxable economic activity or import into Spanish territory triggers mandatory IVA registration in EUR. Optional simplified/cash-basis SME regimes are available only to resident taxpayers with annual turnover below EUR 250,000 and do not defer foreign-exporter registration obligations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Large VAT taxpayers with turnover above EUR 6,000,000 must submit transaction-level invoice feeds to AEAT under the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) through machine-to-machine XML/API weekly or near-real-time. Public-sector e-invoicing requires structured Facturae XML. General B2B e-invoicing is being phased in under the Crea y Crece Law with Verifactu-compliant billing software. Spain does not use real-time fiscal stamping/clearance; auditors rely on electronic registries, hash preservation, and SII reporting systems.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched or transported from Spanish territory to a destination outside the European Union qualify for CAD/IVA zero-rating under Spanish VAT Law Article 21. Claimants must prove physical departure from the EU, possession of a valid export customs declaration accepted by customs, a commercial invoice, transport documentation, and evidence of receipt by the foreign consignee; export-related ancillary services may also qualify if directly linked to the physical export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading, CMR railway/road consignment note, or Air Waybill
Inward Remittance Certificate or other verifiable proof of foreign payment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT and Spanish Customs conduct substantive audits of export evidence. Missing, inconsistent, or fraudulent export documentation disallows zero-rating; VAT becomes due with late-payment interest, and input VAT is clawed back. Tax penalties range from 50% to 150% of the determined amount depending on concealment. False declarations or tax fraud exceeding EUR 120,000 in defrauded tax may trigger criminal liability under the Spanish Criminal Code.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain operates under the Eurozone with full capital account and current account convertibility. Profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are unrestricted subject to Spanish corporate tax compliance and beneficial ownership reporting. No capital controls apply to Spanish SL entities for standard transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Mandatory surrender of foreign currency export proceeds applies only to non-EU transactions and must occur within 15 days of collection at the official Bank of Spain exchange rate. Intra-EU exports require no surrender but demand full commercial documentation for VAT and customs purposes.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Authorized EMI operations are feasible under Spanish Ley 10/2014 with Banco de España oversight. Cross-border digital EMIs require strict authorization, minimum capital of 350000 EUR, and robust AML controls; local EMI licensing is recommended for Spanish SL entities.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote digital onboarding via certified Spanish e-banking platforms is permitted for SL entities. Physical appearance of directors is not mandatory for standard accounts but required for enhanced due diligence or thresholds above 100000 EUR.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Undisclosed beneficial ownership or shell company indicators
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ultimate beneficial owner declaration, corporate structure chart, and source of wealth evidence

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transactions inconsistent with manufacturing business activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed operational contracts, production records, export orders, and audited financial statements

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital via SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 100. Required verifications include shareholder meeting minutes, proof of equity source, and updated share register aligned with Spanish Commercial Registry filings.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements via SWIFT MT103 (purpose code 20) or Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP 600. Intra-EU uses SEPA; non-EU requires full commercial documentation including invoices, certificates of origin, and proof of shipment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Legalization of accounting books, including the journal and inventory and annual accounts book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the end of the financial year; normally by 30 April for a 31 December year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry filing defects or rejection may occur; failure to legalize books may impair evidentiary value and may support accounting or tax sanctions. No automatic strike-off is triggered solely by late book legalization.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts and management report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' General Meeting of the Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end; normally by 30 June for a 31 December year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to approve accounts may delay statutory filing and expose directors to liability for breach of diligence and accounting obligations. No separate government filing fee applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual accounts, management report, and statutory audit report where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after shareholder approval; normally by 31 July for accounts approved on 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry closure generally applies after one year from the filing deadline, preventing registration of most corporate acts. Administrative fines may range from EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000, or up to EUR 300,000 for companies with annual turnover exceeding EUR 6 million. Spanish law does not provide for automatic administrative strike-off solely because annual accounts are filed late.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual declaration of beneficial ownership submitted with the annual accounts deposit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry and the Central Register of Beneficial Ownership where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submitted with each annual accounts deposit; beneficial ownership changes must be updated promptly through the legally prescribed corporate, notarial, or registry channels
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incomplete or inaccurate beneficial ownership information may cause filing rejection, registry closure, compliance restrictions, and potential sanctions under Spanish anti-money laundering legislation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish State Tax Administration Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the first 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the tax year-end; normally 1 to 25 July for a 31 December year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing without prior notice generally attracts a surcharge of 1% plus 1% for each additional complete month of delay, capped at 15%; after prior notice, a penalty generally ranging from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax may apply, subject to statutory reductions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT summary return, Modelo 390, where not exempt from the annual summary requirement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish State Tax Administration Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally filed during the first 30 calendar days of January following the calendar year; the obligation may be replaced or excluded for taxpayers meeting specified reporting conditions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or incorrect filing may trigger fixed tax penalties, generally subject to statutory mitigation and voluntary-disclosure rules. The underlying periodic VAT liability remains payable.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual related-party and controlled-transaction information reporting, including Modelo 232 where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish State Tax Administration Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally during the month following the ten-month period after the tax year-end; normally 1 to 30 November for a 31 December year-end, if applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit or materially incorrect reporting may attract specific tax penalties and may increase transfer-pricing audit exposure. Filing is required only when statutory thresholds or transaction categories are met.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent audit is generally mandatory when the company exceeds at least two of the following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: total assets of EUR 2.85 million, annual net turnover of EUR 5.7 million, and average employees of 50. Mandatory audit also applies in specified cases involving securities, regulated activities, public-interest status, subsidies, public contracts, consolidation, or other statutory triggers.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad) and applicable Spanish accounting regulations. IFRS is generally mandatory for listed groups' consolidated accounts and may apply in other legally permitted cases; it is not the default framework for an ordinary Spanish SL.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must identify and maintain current information on its ultimate beneficial owner. A beneficial ownership declaration is generally submitted with the annual accounts deposit. Changes in ownership, control, or beneficial ownership must be reflected in the Register of Members and reported through the applicable notarial, registry, or Central Register of Beneficial Ownership procedures without waiting for the next annual filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and persons exercising representation
Register of contracts with the sole shareholder, where the company has a sole shareholder
Beneficial ownership information and supporting ownership-control records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 300-1,200 per year for a standard registered-office, mail-handling, and corporate administration package
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 1,500-5,000 for a small non-complex SL subject to mandatory audit; higher for regulated, group, inventory-intensive, or cross-border operations

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, Ley 27/2014, art. 29.1); 15% reduced rate for new companies in their first two fiscal periods with positive taxable income
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% new-company rate (art. 29.1 LIS); capitalization reserve: 15% tax-base reduction for equity increases (art. 25 LIS); SME equalization reserve: 10% reduction for INCN<€1M (art. 105 LIS); R&D credit 25% base (42% combined with personnel/investment add-ons) and 12% technological innovation credit (art. 35 LIS); no industry-specific boba-processing credit
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward since 2015 (art. 26 LIS); annual offset cap: 70% of positive taxable base for taxpayers with net turnover below €1M, 60% for €1M-€20M, 50% above €20M; offsets cannot reduce the taxable base below €1M in each year

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 — annual Corporate Income Tax return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades); mandatory electronic filing via AEAT Sede Electrónica (portal: sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es) using a qualified digital certificate (DNIe, FNMT, or authorized software). Quarterly prepayments: Modelo 202 (calendar-year taxpayers: 1–20 April, 1–20 October, 1–20 November). Related-party information return: Modelo 232.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (Modelo 200); three installment prepayments per year (Modelo 202); annual TP information return (Modelo 232)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Modelo 200 due within 25 calendar days after the six-month period following fiscal year-end; for a 31 December year-end, filing window is 1–25 July. Modelo 202 due 1–20 April (instalment 1), 1–20 October (instalment 2), 1–20 November (instalment 3). Modelo 232 is due on the same day as Modelo 200.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer NIF, legal name (razón social), fiscal year-end date; identifies the SL and the period being declared.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident parent/shareholders do not file on this line; the Spanish SL files its own Modelo 200 under its NIF. Non-resident withholding and income are reported via Modelo 216 (annual WHT summary) and Modelo 210 (self-assessment), not via Modelo 200.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Importe neto de la cifra de negocios (net turnover); determines SME thresholds, installment regime, and documentation obligations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only the Spanish entity’s own turnover. Intercompany sales of canned boba pearls to related distributors must be included at arm’s length prices; any understatement triggers TP audit exposure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Resultado contable antes de impuestos (accounting profit before tax per separate financial statements).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must reconcile with audited financial statements; non-resident shareholders relying on distributions must be aware this is the starting point for tax-base adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compensación de bases imponibles negativas (negative tax-base offset from prior years) and resulting taxable income (base imponible).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Spanish SL offsets prior losses, verify the historical NOL was legally generated and documented; non-resident planning cannot contractually reallocate this statutory right.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cuota íntegra (gross tax liability after credits/deductions) and the final result of the assessment (amount due or refund).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: WHT credits for non-resident-owned entities apply only if the SL itself suffered Spanish WHT; distributions to the non-resident parent are simultaneously reported under the 19% IRNR withholding regime, not on Modelo 200.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Untimely filing without a prior request (art. 27 LGT) carries a surcharge: 5% if filed within 3 months of the deadline, 10% for 3–6 months, 15% for 6–12 months, 20% beyond 12 months, plus late-payment interest (5.0% for 2025) after the first 12 months. Failure to file (art. 198 LGT): fixed penalty of €200 per return (minimum), increased by €100 per omitted element to a maximum of €1,500; proportional penalties of 50%–150% of the under-declared amount apply when the entity files incorrect returns resulting in lower tax (art. 191 LGT). Failure to file Modelo 202 instalments: 50% surcharge on the unpaid instalment amount.
